messages:
olivia: FYI I'm opening a tiny docs PR to modernize the HelloProvision quickstart. Changes: switch examples to REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, add a devcontainer runArg example, and prefer `docker compose` for local runs. PR #4529. Looking for a quick reviewer.
matt: Sounds good. Can you paste the minimal snippets here so I can sanity-check the wording and commands?
olivia: Snippets pasted below (keeps first-run minimal):

```
# .env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_ABCDEF
```

```
# Python example (hello.py)
import os
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-mini', input='Hello, quickstart!')
print(resp.text)
```

olivia: Run locally instruction added: `docker compose up --build hello-provision` so people have one clear command.
rachel: Quick nit: add a one-sentence migration note for folks who used SESSION_TOKEN in older quickstarts: "If you previously followed cookie/session examples, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment; server-side cookie auth is still supported for Dedicated/Private—see enterprise auth docs." Keep it non-alarming and link to /enterprise/auth.
matt: Also include the devcontainer example for Codespaces/VS Code: "\"runArgs\": [\"-e\", \"REDWOOD_API_KEY=${localEnv:REDWOOD_API_KEY}\"]" in devcontainer.json. And maybe one short sentence about storing keys securely (KMS/secret manager) for production.
olivia: Added both changes and a short sentence about secret stores with a link to the security page. Pushed patch and enabled link-check CI.
ops-bot: CI status for PR #4529: lint: passed, link-check: passed, preview: https://deploy-preview-4529--docs.redwood.ai
rachel: LGTM aside from a tiny phrasing tweak I pushed. This is low risk.
matt: Approved. I'll merge and run a staging smoke test.
olivia: Thanks! Merged. I'll follow up with a micro-e2e that runs the quickstart container in CI and add a short migration note in the migration guide next sprint.
